episodes.214501: A backdoor front pushed through northeast and east-central NM and ended up along the east slopes of the central mountain chain come midday July 31st. Higher moisture behind the front, and lift along the front resulted in thunderstorm development across the central mountain chain during the early afternoon. Storms congealed into a line as they moved east and southeast across the eastern highlands and plains resulting in severe thunderstorm wind gusts near Cuero in Guadalupe County, Tucumcari and Clayton Municipal Airports, and a mesonet station in far northeast Lincoln County. The line also resulted in thunderstorm wind damage at a CoCoRaHS observer's residence south of Fort Sumner. The line of thunderstorms moved southeast into west Texas during the mid to late evening hours while the backdoor front pushed through the gaps of the central mountain chain resulting in gusty east canyon winds across the Santa Fe and Albuquerque Metros.
episodes.214642: Heavy rainfall, totaling 3 to 4 inches, fell across part of the city of Tuscaloosa, resulting in flooding issues and stranded vehicles along McFarland Blvd.
episodes.214747: By the middle of the afternoon of the 31st, a cold front stalled out across the extreme southern Texas Panhandle. Strong surface heating ahead of the front allowed storms to develop along the leading edge of the front creating severe wind gusts in Childress County. A second round of storms came during the evening hours from the west. Thunderstorms initially developed off of the higher terrain of eastern New Mexico into the Raton Mesa. As these storms progressed southeastward they eventually grew upscale along numerous outflow boundaries spreading into the South Plains. A dry sub-cloud layer allowed these storms to become outflow dominant creating numerous severe wind gusts through the late evening hours.
episodes.214954: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms produced several wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.215450: Thunderstorms moved across northern Kansas late evening on July 30 into the early morning hours of the 31st, producing scattered 55-70 mph gusts and some wind damage.
episodes.215951: A weakening frontal boundary over southeast Georgia shifted southward and stalled along the I-10 corridor on the afternoon of July 30th. An unstable airmass, high moisture (PWATs 2+ inches) and lift from the stalled front enhanced wet microburst activity and localized flooding. On July 31st, similar setup as July 30th but with some drier air in the area aiding in isolated downburst development.
episodes.215983: Heavy rainfall led to some reported flash flooding and flooded roadways in the vicinity of Ellicott, Peyton and Falcon.
episodes.215989: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed along a weak cold front from southwestern Oklahoma into western-north Texas on the evening of the 31st. The strongest thunderstorms produced strong to locally severe wind gusts across this area.
episodes.216017: During the late evening hours of July 30 into the early morning hours of July 31, 2026, a cluster of thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts across northeast Nebraska, while additional thunderstorms produced damaging winds in southeast Nebraska.||Thunderstorm development across northeast Nebraska was forced by a cold front diving southward across the region into a modestly unstable airmass. The thunderstorm complex initially developed along the central Nebraska���South Dakota border before tracking southeastward into the area. As the complex pushed through Norfolk, NE, between 7:43 PM and 7:49 PM CST, several wind damage reports were received, including a 2-foot diameter tree downed, snapped and uprooted trees, and large broken tree branches. Emergency management noted that the damage was oriented west-to-east across a broad area, indicative of a downburst.||The thunderstorm complex gradually pushed southeastward into southeast Nebraska and southwest Iowa during the early morning hours of July 31, producing a measured wind gust of 58 mph near Preston, NE, at 12:28 AM CST before tracking into northeast Kansas and northwest Missouri.
episodes.216088: Thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon hours of July 30 along the Cherry County and South Dakota border. As this activity tracked to the southeast, it morphed into a line of severe thunderstorms. As the afternoon progressed, a line of storms extended from south central Cherry County into western Boyd and northwestern Holt counties. This line tracked southeast into central Nebraska clearing Custer and eastern Lincoln County by 9 PM CDT. Thunderstorm wind gusts to 80 MPH were reported Near Brownlee along with flash flooding in Valentine. Hail up to ping pong ball size was reported in Stapleton.
episodes.216276: A localized severe thunderstorm wind gusts occurred in Bear Lake County.
episodes.216286: A storm system moved across the area during the late afternoon and evening hours on the 31st and brought scattered storms to the area during the afternoon and evening. These storms produced several clouds.  One of these storms produced a tornado near the Cedar Rapids Eastern Iowa Airport. This tornado was rated EFU because there was no visible damage.
episodes.216424: Storms produced heavy rainfall on July 30th into the early morning of July 31st, with a number of reports of rainfall at or in excess of 5 inches centered across Day and Roberts counties. Heavy rainfall resulted in flooding and stalled cars in the city of Aberdeen with the Official National Weather Service observation of 2.55 inches. Flooding also impacted the cities of Pierre and Fort Pierre including portions of US Highway 14. Multiple roads and county/state highways were closed north of US Highway 12 in Day county due to water over the road, including Highway 33 near Roslyn and Highway 27 near Pierpont. The highest reported measured total was 6.90 inches by the CoCoRaHS observer 6.6 miles east northeast of Grenville (Day County).||There was also a brief period of minor flooding along the Little Minnesota River near Peever, after 5.8 inches was recorded by the COOP observer in Sisseton, and 6.34 was measured by the CoCoRaHS observer 10 miles east northeast of Sisseton.
episodes.216454: A long duration rain event resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms from overnight July 30th into the 31st and lasted through the afternoon. Rainfall rates were generally under 0.5 to 1 inch per hour, which limited the flooding impacts across the region. Given the persistence of light to moderate rain, around 3 to 5 inches fell across the Minnesota River Valley in southwest MN, with pockets of 5 to 7 inches. The worst impacts were reported just north of St Peter, MN where a small mudslide resulted in a partial closure of US169 during the morning on the 31st.
episodes.216496: Broad northwesterly flow atop of rich moisture allowed for storms to develop across the plains. A stronger storm in Baca County produced severe winds.
episodes.216497: Another day with broad northwest flow overtop of moisture allowed for scattered thunderstorms to develop across south central Colorado. One cluster of storms across southeastern El Paso County became strong and produced large hail.
episodes.216643: During the evening hours on the 30th, a few supercell thunderstorms moved southeast across portions of southwest Nebraska. One such supercell thunderstorm clipped far northeast portions of Hitchcock County with a 69 mph wind gust.
episodes.216788: An isolated thunderstorm impacted Hutchinson during the early morning hours of July 31st. Hutchinson Regional Airport recorded a wind gust of 58 mph from the storm, but no damage was reported.
episodes.216966: Two rounds of severe weather impacted the region the last two days of July.
episodes.216969: A storm brought damaging winds to Campbell county.
episodes.217181: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the east central Florida coastline.
episodes.217207: During the afternoon a broken line of severe thunderstorms moved southeast through central and southeast Missouri. On its track, a few cells produced 3 tornadoes as well as tree and structural damage.
episodes.217285: Strong to severe thunderstorms off the Atlantic coast of South Florida produced waterspout activity.
